thread.title: Why Coherent Trades At A Steep Discount - Coherent, Inc. (NASDAQ:COHR)

author: Chris Lau
title: Why Coherent Trades At A Steep Discount - Coherent, Inc. (NASDAQ:COHR)
text:
Financial metrics are one easy way to characterize a stock as a value investment. For Coherent ( COHR ), the stock’s low multiple of 15.4 times earnings and 10 times forward earnings would lead a value investor to ask why the stock is inexpensive. After the stock fell again, from $180 to $128 and down 30% in the quarter, the earnings report in the fourth quarter revealed a few disappointments.
Execution errors at one of its manufacturing facilities in Germany in relation to an ERP implementation hurt results in Q4. Macro headwinds from the weakening China market conditions did not help matters, either. And while management took remedial actions – process change, re-aligning responsibilities and personnel – China is still the biggest unknown for the company.
U.S. tariffs hurt the photonics business, offset by high fab plant utilization rates, due to the release of two OLED-equipped iPhones from Apple ( AAPL ). Unlike Lumentum ( LITE ), Qorvo ( QRVO ) and AMS cutting output, Coherent is not facing the same order cuts from Apple. It is still postponing shipment and moving it to the next quarter due to a customer request. In the semiconductor space, price declines for memory in the range of 10-15% could be offset by foreign investment in the Chinese chip industry.
Investors are already well aware of the lack of pricing power for chip firms like Micron Technology ( MU ) or Applied Materials ( AMAT ). The forecast from Coherent is consistent with that of Applied: the firm is cutting its fiscal 2019 revenue outlook by 8-12%, but believes the second half of 2019 will be stronger than the first half. Coherent will cut costs and CapEx by $10 million-$15 million to adjust for the lower demand-supply equilibrium. It will also buy back up to $250 million in the company’s common stock to a maximum of $75 million per quarter.
COHR data by YCharts
Revenue Mix In the fourth quarter, microelectronics made up 53% of revenue. Materials processing was 27%, OEM components and instrumentation was 14% and scientific and government was 6%. Geographically, Asia accounted for around 61% of Q4’s revenue. Coherent’s balance sheet does not show any concerns: cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $311 million while debt was $431 million.
Microelectronics a Drag Just as the microelectronics giant STMicroelectronics ( STM ) forecast weaker market conditions, Coherent’s lower revenue guide of $375 million to $395 million is due mostly to the drop in electronics. Order cancellations and push-outs in China are driving demand lower.
Investors with a short-term time frame would wish that the U.S. and China would agree on something tangible on November 30, during the G20 meeting, but chances of that happening are very low. Even with the tariffs in place, Coherent still forecasts business in 2020 will improve over 2019. In effect, 2019 will be an inflection point when the company faces lower sales and profit declines offset by cost cuts.
Valuation Based on the future cash flow value, COHR stock is worth $186 , well above the $128 closing price on November 23.
Source: simplywall.st
Analysts are just as bullish. Based on the seven analysts covering Coherent, the average target price is around $183, implying an upside of 43% (source: tipranks ). The wide discount on Coherent and the expected future value of the stock highlights how excessively negative the market is. China’s downtrend might get worse if the U.S. follows through on its threat to levy tariffs. If tariffs are hiked again, management may have to lower its FY2019 guidance.
Coherent is a leading laser supplier whose prospects could rebound in Asia. At these valuations, the stock has a big discount that prices in the potential headwinds ahead.
